nfl.oneThing: The Cardinals are finalising a trade that sends QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens, while Baltimore is dealing with another injury to Lamar Jackson.

headlines.title: Brissett heads to Baltimore as Arizona goes all in on Minshew
headlines.summary: The Cardinals are finalising a trade sending quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Baltimore has already lost Tyler Huntley to a right toe sprain, and Lamar Jackson has suffered yet another injury. Jackson's contract runs out after the 2027 season. The Ravens are 4-4 and 10th in the AFC, 1.0 games behind the last playoff spot.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore is adding a quarterback while Jackson and Huntley are hurt, and it sits just one game outside the AFC's last playoff spot.

headlines.title: Bears add Simmons and Colts keep trading veterans before the deadline
headlines.summary: The trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. CBS Sports calls Chicago's addition of Jeffery Simmons a blockbuster. Indianapolis has traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jonathan Taylor is at the centre of trade talks with multiple teams, but Shane Steichen says the running back will keep his usual role. ESPN's deadline preview also says the Chiefs are looking for a dependable wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes.
headlines.whyItMatters: Chicago is 6-2 and fifth in the NFC, so it is adding to a contender. The Colts are 2-6 and building draft capital.

headlines.title: Jack Campbell says he has full lower-body movement
headlines.summary: Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell said in a statement on Wednesday that he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with his upper body. He was carted off early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 19-15 win over the Vikings after a neck injury, and he remains in hospital. He was alert and breathing when he was taken off the field. Dan Campbell said it was powerful that the linebacker gave the update himself.
headlines.whyItMatters: Detroit is 5-2 and sixth in the NFC, and it is preparing for the Dolphins without its All-Pro linebacker.

teamNews.title: Porter questionable for the 49ers game
teamNews.text: Starting cornerback Darien Porter did not practise on Wednesday after leaving the Jets game on the first play with a groin injury. Kubiak says he will be monitored. If Porter can't play, rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses are likely to rotate, as they did against the Jets.

nba.oneThing: The Warriors have stopped paying Kristaps Porzingis his $20 million salary while they try to trade the contract before the February 11 deadline.

headlines.title: Warriors stop paying Porzingis as they look for a trade
headlines.summary: The Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary. League sources told ESPN that Golden State has ruled he is not rendering services. Porzingis has been away from the team since late September while dealing with health issues, and he is reportedly leaning toward ending his career. The Warriors have no plans to void the contract, and Porzingis is not disputing the withheld money. RealGM reports he would be motivated to agree to a buyout if he were traded.
headlines.whyItMatters: Golden State wants to keep its trade options open until February 11. A rival could take on the near-expiring salary, and the price depends on what the Warriors attach.

headlines.title: Sixers and Pistons top the East
headlines.summary: Philadelphia is 7-1 after its 126–107 win over Chicago, its fourth straight win. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era has started well for the 76ers. Next they face the 6-1 Pistons on national TV, a matchup of the top two teams in the East. Tyrese Maxey is averaging 29.1 points a game, behind only Luka Dončić and Stephen Curry. Coach Nick Nurse is being urged to give more minutes to Labaron Philon Jr.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Sixers and Pistons are first and second in the East, so this is an early test for both. Wins over Eastern rivals now can help the playoff seeding later.

contextCard.title: How NBA buyouts work
contextCard.body: When a team wants to move a player's salary, it can trade him and sometimes agree a buyout as well. The player gives up part of his remaining salary so he can leave the team and become a free agent, often to join a contender. It's a common way for a contract to be cleared when a trade alone won't work.
